- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.4) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% relative to prior 30d mean.
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% above recent 10d high), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above peak or use 10d moving average as ceiling.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.8) and price is trending up, model frequently overcorrects; apply downward bias of 1–3% to avoid overbought overreaction.
- When true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 10d moving average), model tends to lag; adjust forecast to align with 10d MA or 14d SMA for next 5–7 days.
- If sentiment is mixed (0.4–0.8) and price is volatile, model often fails to capture short-term reversals; use sentiment-weighted average (e.g., 0.7×sentiment + 0.3×price) for next 3–5 days.
- For 30d forecasts, if true outcome is consistently below model by >3% over 5+ days, apply a “reversion penalty” — reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day until convergence with observed trend.
